title: PR surgery scratchpad
content:
TL;DR
Quick, messy scratchpad for PR 'surgery' — what to fix, what to push to a follow-up PR, and a few small refactor experiments to try later. Not polished. Use as checklist when triaging medium/large PRs.

Context / motivation
- I keep seeing PRs that try to do 3 things at once: perf tweak + API surface change + refactor. Hard to review.
- Goal: separate minimal safe change (can ship) from deeper cleanup (follow-up) and note quick wins.
- This doc is my running shorthand — copy bits into PR comments or new issues.

How I do a quick "PR surgery" (10–30m pass)
(1) Safety & correctness (must fix before merge)
  - [ ] Does CI pass? If flaky, mark with retries and note failing test names.
  - [ ] Any new public API shape? (breaking-change label?) If yes -> separate PR or detailed migration notes.
  - [ ] Missing input validation or unsafe nil derefs — add guard or test.

(2) Observability & debugging (high importance)
  - [ ] Add or preserve tracing spans for hot paths (span names: service:handler, runtime:generate).
  - [ ] Prom metrics: create/update counters for "cache_miss", "batch_size_histogram" and gauge for worker_pool_size.
  - [ ] Log levels: no new WARNs for normal flow. If adding WARN, include reason + remediation.

(3) Performance hygiene (fast wins)
  - [ ] Avoid copying large tensors/byte arrays — prefer references or move semantics.
  - [ ] Check for accidental sync points (await/lock inside tight loop). Flag potential hotspot.
  - [ ] Batching: confirm new path respects batching policy; add a small microbenchmark if behavior changed.

(4) Code health & readability
  - [ ] New functions should be < 60 lines and single responsibility. If not, propose decomposition in comment.
  - [ ] Naming: prefer explicit over abbreviated (eg kvCache vs cache).
  - [ ] Inline comments: explain non-obvious math/heuristics (quant thresholds, cache eviction heuristics).

(5) What to move to a follow-up PR (non-blocking but desirable)
  - [ ] Large refactors that touch many files (split out).
  - [ ] Non-critical API ergonomics or docstring cleanups.
  - [ ] Adding new config knobs — can add later with rollout plan.
  - [ ] Instrumentation improvements that require dashboards/dataschema changes.

Common patterns & micro-templates for comments
- "Safety: move runtime-wide retry logic to a helper (XXX) or add unit tests around retry backoff. Not a blocker if test coverage added."
- "Perf: single-token path currently copies KV cache; short-term: keep as-is but file follow-up INF-xxx to remove copy; long-term rewrite in runtime/cache.v2"
- "Observability: please add span 'kv-cache:hit' with attribute 'model_variant' so we can break down cache effectiveness by model."

Mini-refactor idea (note to self) — KV cache acceptor pattern
- Problem: many callers do ad-hoc locking + copying before access. Leads to contention and hidden copies.
- Proposal sketch: introduce cache.AcquireRead(handle) -> (view, release) where view is immutable slice/ref and release is deferable. Implement lightweight RC inside cache layer.
- Migration path: wrap existing hot callers first (generate path), ship behind feature flag, measure latency and allocations.
- Risks: complexity in ensuring view invalidation when evicting; need unit tests for concurrent access.

Small code snippet idea (pseudocode)
- keep as text in PR comment, not committed in this PR:

  // Acquire read view (no copy)
  v, release := cache.AcquireRead(key)
  defer release()
  // use v bytes directly

Checklist for PR author (copy into PR description)
- [ ] Added tests for new behavior (unit + small integration)
- [ ] Benchmarks or perf notes attached if relevant (attach flame graph if >5% regression)
- [ ] Added tracing spans and metrics where appropriate
- [ ] Logged on error paths with context (request-id, model-id)

Open questions for reviewers (put in review comment)
- Is splitting this into two PRs more helpful? (safety/perf vs cleanup)
- Any concerns with adding metric names I proposed? (naming collisions)
- Do we need an entry in rollout playbook for toggling this feature?

Follow-ups to file after merge (examples)
- Create follow-up ticket: "refactor: introduce cache.AcquireRead" + rough ETA.
- Dashboard: add cache_miss% per model_variant in infra dashboard.
- Benchmark job: add a microbenchmark to perf-ci that runs synthetic workload for the changed codepath.

Notes-to-self (short snippets)
- Don't let PRs push both the runtime API change and docs in same PR. Docs can be follow-up only if API experimental.
- If a test is flaky locally but passes on CI, run it 10x locally with -race to reproduce.
- When in doubt: leave smaller change, file follow-up issue with link to PR.

Recent triage snippets (examples I left in previous PRs)
- "LGTM aside from small nit: extract tokenization logic to helper for reuse (will add in follow-up). Marking as non-blocking."
- "Major: avoid creating new ephemeral buffer per request — flips allocations. Suggest reuse pool or reuse byte.Buffer with Reset()."

References (links I frequently paste)
- PR style guide: https://confluence.redwood/engineering/pr-style-guide
- Benchmark template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/blob/main/README.md

End — keep this short and noisy. Duplicate useful lines into PR comments so they persist.
